verdict.rationale: Rippling's own docs say that when someone leaves, it automatically updates access, permissions and groups. They also describe real-time revocation across SCIM/SAML-connected apps with "no SCIM lag," which covers automated, near-immediate deprovisioning on offboarding. The evidence never mentions terminating active sessions, and all support is vendor marketing copy. missing for 10: documented active-session revocation on deactivation, per-app deprovisioning detail and coverage limits, independent or hands-on corroboration of immediacy.

support.subject: As a security engineer, offboarding is one action — deactivating a user kills their sessions and deprovisions their accounts across connected apps immediately

citations.quote: When roles changes or someone leaves, Rippling automatically updates access, permissions, and groups.
Rippling monitors your org in real time and automatically provisions or revokes access based on role changes, risk signals, and company policy.
so access always reflects reality, with no SCIM lag, no stale syncs
to custom SCIM and SAML apps
